invariant-end-page-inclusive-zero-size:
memory page-range helpers (native/angr/src/memory/mod.rs) must be reached via `end_page_inclusive(addr,size)` / `end_page_exclusive(addr,size)`, never an inlined formula. The workspace [profile.release] leaves overflow-checks OFF, so both directions wrap silently in production:
(1) UNDERFLOW, size==0 (angr-9ke6b.99): `addr+size-1` wraps to u64::MAX and check_perms_range iterates ~4.5e15 pages — a hang. Rejected as MemoryError::ZeroSize. Reachable: `_pending_memory_load` (exploration/pending_api.rs) forwards a Python-supplied size unchecked; on the store side `size = value.width()/8` is 0 for any sub-byte BV. A second, earlier underflow exists per load — the wider-symbolic extract's `size*8-1` (u32) inside load_concrete — hence the explicit size==0 early-returns in load_concrete / load_concrete_lazy_inner *in addition to* the helper.
(2) OVERFLOW, addr near u64::MAX (angr-03vl4.34/.35): `addr+size-1` wraps to an end_page BELOW start_page, so `start_page..=end_page` and check_perms_range are both EMPTY — every mapped-page and permission check silently skipped — and the byte loops' wrapping `Address` addition then walks down through 0 and reads/writes a real low page. Rejected as MemoryError::OutOfBounds. Reachable, not theoretical: `write_fallback_max` is the default (concretize.rs, matching Python's SimConcretizationStrategyMax), so an under-constrained store pointer concretizes to exactly u64::MAX.
Both helpers are fallible; end_page_exclusive is NOT exempt (its old doc claimed 'only ever adds, so cannot underflow' — true, but it overflows). Three rules future work must keep: (a) `addr+size == 2^64` (a region ending exactly at the top of the address space, e.g. mapping the last page) is LEGAL, not an overflow — end_page_exclusive special-cases it to (u64::MAX>>12)+1, and any caller-level guard must therefore check `addr.checked_add(size - 1)`, not `checked_add(size)`, or it over-rejects the last page; (b) the infallible-signature callers `map`/`unmap`/`add_lazy_region` skip-and-warn on overflow via silent_default!(cat_c) rather than CLAMPING to the last page — clamping would turn `map(0, u64::MAX)` from a fast no-op into 2^52 page insertions, i.e. a Python-reachable OOM; (c) BECAUSE (b) makes map/unmap skip silently, every caller that REPORTS SUCCESS after calling them needs its own overflow guard — otherwise it returns success for a mapping that was never made. syscalls/mmap.rs::do_mmap hit exactly this (angr-03vl4.68): its `if !is_fixed && range_collides(..)` gate meant the MAP_FIXED branch never reached range_collides's checked_add guard, so a page-aligned addr near u64::MAX under the MAX_MAP_SIZE cap returned Ok(candidate) having mapped nothing. When adding a new memory-mapping caller, ask whether its success path can outlive a skipped map().
invariant-enum-indexed-parallel-arrays: Enum-discriminant-indexed parallel arrays are a panic-grade cardinality-rot shape in this crate: an enum with #[repr(usize)] plus a hand-written NUM_* const, hand-written [AtomicU64; NUM_*] initializers, and a hand-written [&str; NUM_*] name table, where a dispatcher does TABLE[variant as usize]. Adding a variant compiles clean, keeps any 'tables agree with NUM_*' test green (it never cross-checks the enum's arity), and panics out of bounds on first use. Both known instances are now macro-generated: symbolic/query_class.rs::QueryClass (query_classes!, angr-6cp06.49) and symbolic/stats.rs::CheckSite (check_sites!, angr-6cp06.89). Fix pattern: one 'Variant => "stats_key"' list drives the enum, the NUM_ const (as [$($key),+].len() on a fresh array literal -- NAMES.len() would be a const cycle), every counter array ([const { AtomicU64::new(0) }; NUM_]), the name table, and a const _ block asserting discriminant == declaration index; drop explicit = 0..N discriminants since an implicit fieldless #[repr(usize)] enum numbers from 0 by definition. The two macros were deliberately NOT hoisted into one shared macro -- CheckSite's family splits across the vex-engine-z3 cfg, has two counter arrays not one, and uses different visibilities, so parameterizing over all three costs more than the list it would share. Distinct from CLAUDE.md's 'never describe a set by its cardinality' comment rule -- that one rots prose, this one crashes. When you meet a new NUM_<THING> const, check whether it is hand-synced against an enum.
invariant-epsilon-closure-cache-panic: automaton epsilon-closure cache contract (angr-9ke6b.193, 2026-08-03): EpsilonNFA::epsilon_closure (native/angr/src/automaton/epsilon_nfa.rs) now panics via a let-else with a descriptive message when a state id is >= the cached closure vec's length; it used to bounds-check-and-skip. Adds a THIRD tier to the assert-hardening rule of thumb from invariant-move-on-symbol-epsilon-result: (1) Result when PyO3-reachable with few callers, (2) debug_assert! for a pure-internal worklist invariant that would only mis-step, (3) unconditional panic! when skipping would produce a SILENTLY WRONG result in release builds — here a dropped state means a wrong closure means a wrong DFA, and debug_assert! alone would leave release builds silently wrong. epsilon_closure is pub but consumed only inside automaton:: (subset_construction + move_on_symbol + is_empty), so no PyO3 PanicException concern. The panic message names both causes (stale cache after a mutation that failed to clear epsilon_closures, or a caller-supplied non-state id) because both are bugs. Tested by epsilon_nfa_tests.rs::test_epsilon_closure_panics_on_stale_cache, which reaches into the private num_states field (tests are a child module via #[path]) to simulate the invalidation bug no public API can produce.

invariant-eval-upto-canonical-order: eval_upto/eval_upto_wide (native/angr/src/symbolic/solving_ops.rs) return witnesses in CANONICAL ASCENDING ORDER as of angr-op0dn.10.1 (commit 3f5e2a782). As of angr-9ke6b.142 (commit 0277e87a6) the enumeration machinery — warm-model seed, exclude-loop, trailing sort_unstable — lives in ONE shared helper, SymContext::enumerate_distinct<T: Ord>(ast, n, extract, exclusion_of); the two public fns keep only their concrete fast paths, the deterministic-mode branch (eval_upto only), the query_class scope, and the closures. So the sort is now in enumerate_distinct, not at the callsites. Presentation-only: the enumerated SET is decided by the exclude-loop and the ovqja.4 warm-model seed, so the sort cannot change WHICH values come back, only their order. For eval_upto_wide every witness is exactly `width` bits, so all byte vectors are the same length and big-endian lexicographic sort == numeric sort (see u128_to_be_bytes_width). INVARIANT for future work: any short-circuit or early-return added inside eval_upto (e.g. an M1 trivial-decide tier) must land ABOVE the helper call / sort, or it reintroduces order nondeterminism. Truncated case (n < #feasible) still returns an arbitrary Z3-chosen SUBSET — canonical subset choice is M2.2 (angr-op0dn.10.2). Tests: context_tests/solver_queries.rs::test_eval_upto_canonical_order / test_eval_upto_wide_canonical_order.
invariant-execution-config-not-concretiz: ExecutionConfig (native/angr/src/callbacks/config.rs) is the deferred-fork/prefetch loop config ONLY -- it is NOT where concretization or branch selection is configured. THREE of its #[pyo3(get,set)] knobs have now been found dead and deleted: (1)+(2) in 32b9901b1 (angr-9ke6b.16/.17) -- max_concretization_range (default 65536) had no reader anywhere; the real symbolic-address bounds are AddressConcretizer::{read_range_limit,write_range_limit} in concretize.rs (1024/128, SimOption-driven; the struct is AddressConcretizer, there is no ConcretizerConfig type) -- extend THAT struct, never re-add a knob here; and branch_policy + the whole BranchPolicy pyclass enum (TakeTrue/TakeFalse/TakeFallthrough/Alternate, registered via m.add_class in engine.rs) was read only by __repr__ and its own unit tests -- the fork path always continues down the true branch and defers the other side (see use_deferred_forks). VEXInterpreter::branch_counter went with it. (3) in 4756de8d3 (angr-c7xno.5) -- enable_stride_detection was a separate field from AddressConcretizer::enable_stride_detection (hardcoded true in its Default, read by the stride paths); AddressConcretizer is built without ever seeing an ExecutionConfig (VEXInterpreter::with_config, RustSimState::with_solver_endian) and VEXInterpreter::set_config only assigns self.config, so the Python setter was a silent no-op. LESSON for the rest of that audit-bead class: a #[pyo3(get,set)] field with no Rust reader is worse than dead code -- it is a silent no-op in the PUBLIC API, so removal beats wiring unless a second mechanism does not already own the behavior. GENERALIZED CHECK when auditing any config struct: a field name that also exists on a *different* struct is the tell -- grep the name and confirm the reader reads THIS struct's copy, not the twin's. All three scope decisions are recorded in the ExecutionConfig doc comment so the knobs do not get re-added.
invariant-extend-no-narrow: op_zero_extend/op_sign_extend (native/angr/src/solver/handle_api.rs #[pymethods] -- moved out of solver.rs by angr-9ke6b.205, along with reject_extend_narrowing itself) call reject_extend_narrowing() to raise PyValueError when to_width < source width, instead of zero_extend_into silently returning a wider BV (which surfaced far away as a Z3 sort error / silent eq-False). zero_extend_into + sign_extend_into are now symmetric: both debug_assert!(to_width>=width) with == early-return. No internal caller narrows via extend (VEX widening ops, procedures all widen; strtol guards with 'if w<bits'). Width lookup uses table.with_value(a_id,|bv|bv.width()) -- no clone. angr-ph300.38.
invariant-external-width-bounds-at-bound:
Any width / bit-range / offset chosen by a caller OUTSIDE the engine must be bound-checked at the trust boundary itself, via the shared helpers in native/angr/src/symbolic/width_guards.rs (MAX_BV_WIDTH = 1<<20, check_bv_width, check_extract_bounds). Two boundaries call them: solver/handle_api.rs (the claripy-bypass handle API: create_symbolic/create_concrete/op_zero_extend/op_sign_extend width cap, op_extract range, op_truncate via reject_truncate_widening — the mirror of the older reject_extend_narrowing — and op_concat via reject_concat_overflow) and claripy_bridge/import.rs (the Extract arm via check_extract_bounds; the BVV and BVS arms via check_bv_width; the ZeroExt/SignExt arms via the file-local extended_width helper — angr-0jh0j.8; the Concat arm via that same helper applied to its accumulator at EVERY step of the operand loop, not once at the end — angr-5mnx3.9). Add new external-input constructors to that list rather than re-deriving the conditions.

WHY the downstream debug_assert!s are not enough — this is a SCOPE LIMIT on debug-assert-triage-policy class (1) ('width/arity checks in value_ops.rs kept debug-only because a width mismatch is already rejected at the Python boundary by symbolic/table.rs's binary-op macro'). That rationale only covers binary-op width MISMATCH between two operands. It does NOT cover a unary width ARGUMENT: value_ops::truncate_into's debug_assert!(to_width <= width), value_ops::zero_extend_into's debug_assert!(to_width >= self.width()) and drive_extract's debug_assert!(high < width) guard values that arrive from Python with no macro in the path, and all compile out of the shipped release profile (see invariant-assert-not-debug-assert-in-release). Consequence when unchecked (angr-c7xno.92/.93/.94): low>high wraps the result width high-low+1 to near-u32::MAX under release's no-overflow-checks arithmetic; to_width>source or to_width==0 builds an Extract past the end; both reach Z3_mk_extract as invalid-argument calls, i.e. a SIGABRT under panic='abort' that Python cannot catch. An absurd width instead defers to a multi-gigabit Z3 sort allocation (hang/OOM).

GOTCHA 1: an op whose result width is DERIVED, not passed, is the easy one to miss — no width argument means no obvious place to call check_bv_width, so op_concat sat unguarded while every named-width sibling was covered (angr-0jh0j.73), and import.rs's ZeroExt/SignExt computed val.width() + extend_bits with a bare + (angr-0jh0j.8). The scan question is 'can this op make the width grow?', not 'does this op take a width?'. And the scan has to be run per-BOUNDARY as well as per-op: fixing op_concat at the handle-API boundary (angr-0jh0j.73) and ZeroExt/SignExt at the claripy boundary (angr-0jh0j.8) still left import.rs's Concat arm unguarded through two more review rounds, because each fix swept its own file. When you guard a derived-width op, grep the OTHER boundary for the same op name before closing. Derive with checked_add and REFUSE on overflow (never saturate — see invariant-overflow-fix-refuse-not-saturate-identities), then check_bv_width the sum: h = op_concat(h, h) doubles per call, reaching the cap in ~21 calls and wrapping u32 in ~32, which leaves an Expression whose recorded width is small and wrong while its Z3 AST is enormous — corrupting even the later check_extract_bounds that validates against it. A wrapped ZeroExt is worse still: new_width comes out SMALLER than the source, so the 'extension' silently narrows.

GOTCHA 2: width 0 is a SUPPORTED degenerate concrete RustBV (tests/engines/rust/test_plugins.py::test_create_concrete_zero_width_round_trip round-trips it), so check_bv_width deliberately allows 0 — do not add a nonzero-width check to the creation path. It is only rejected for op_truncate of a wider source, where to_width-1 wraps. See invariant-rustbv-zero-width for the obligation that places on each op's concrete arm.

GOTCHA 3: guarding the arm is not enough if a FAST PATH bypasses it. claripy_bridge::import::try_extract_bvv is a cheap shortcut for the same 'BVV' arm, consumed by five solver.rs call sites — one of which (RustSolverContext::eval_batch) builds RustBV::concrete(value, width) from it. Guarding only the arm would have let the shortcut accept exactly what the general path refuses. Any such shortcut must apply the same check (there: check_bv_width(...).ok()? so an over-cap width falls back to the general, error-reporting path). When adding a guard, grep for the op's fast path as well as its arm.
invariant-extract-args-no-silent-placeho: ExtractionError (native/angr/src/arch/calling_conventions.rs, re-exported from arch::mod) has exactly THREE variants: SpSymbolic (state.get_sp().as_u64() failed), StackUnmapped{arg_index,addr} (memory_load failed for that slot), RegisterOverflow{requested,available} (ABI has no stack window — syscall ABIs other than MIPS O32). There is ONE argument-extraction implementation: exploration::helpers::extract_args_with_abi, which walks a RustSimState using an ArgExtractAbi borrow; core_outcome_cc and helpers' extract_procedure_args/extract_syscall_args are thin adapters over it. Do NOT reintroduce a second copy on the CallingConvention trait — the old trait method extract_args (over a bare RegisterFile + Option<&SymbolicMemory>) and its MemoryUnavailable variant were DELETED in angr-9iny6 (2026-08-08) precisely because they were a structurally-parallel duplicate with no production caller, kept alive only by their own tests. CallingConvention now supplies ABI facts only (arg/syscall register windows, pointer_size, stack_arg_offset, return/link registers). Never fabricate silent placeholders on either the error or the register-overflow path: every failure must fall through to the Python callback.

invariant-fake-ast-must-hash-by-content: Any Python stand-in object handed to claripy_to_rustbv (a 'Fake' AST fixture in Rust unit tests, or any duck-typed AST) MUST define __hash__ content-addressed — (op, length, child hashes) — never 'return id(self)'. claripy_bridge/cache.rs's AST_CACHE is a thread-local LRU keyed on ast.__hash__(); its doc states the precondition explicitly (content hashes survive collection, ids are recycled). A fixture hashing by id lets a Fake built after an earlier one was dropped inherit the freed node's cached RustBV, producing a WRONG value with no error — angr-5o2v7 saw claripy_bridge::import::import_tests::test_bool_fold_refuses_mismatched_operand_widths read the empty-And identity (1) back for empty-Or (0), intermittently, depending on pymalloc address reuse. It presented as a 'flaky test' for six clean runs before reproducing in the ralph gate. The shared fixture now lives in one const, FAKE_AST_CLASS in claripy_bridge/import_tests.rs; reuse it rather than re-inlining a class body. The same hazard applies to any future cache keyed on a Python hash.
invariant-feature-gated-modules-unlinted: CORRECTION (iter148, supersedes the iter147 claim): feature-gated Rust modules ARE covered by a CI lint gate. ci.yml's rust_check runs 'cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings' from the workspace root, so fuzzer/, icicle.rs, automaton/ and libvex-ffi all get linted at PR time. The local dev command in CLAUDE.md's workflow (plain 'cargo clippy --all-targets') does NOT enable them, which is why a feature-gated red can look invisible locally. Practical rule: before committing a change to any #[cfg(feature = ...)] module, run clippy with --all-features (matching CI), not the default-feature command. The 17 unreachable_pub errors this memory previously blamed on a missing gate were in fact a REAL red CI gate, introduced by d4fef1ef3 (angr-9ke6b.50, multiple-pymethods) whose scoped-#[allow(unreachable_pub)] sweep skipped src/fuzzer/; fixed in angr-fggug by applying the same scoped allow to ClientStats, PyOnDiskCorpus, PyHavocMutator, PyDeterministicMutator. ADDENDUM (angr-aygsg): the gate has the mirror-image blind spot. --all-features compiles every feature-only caller, so it can NEVER see dead_code that exists only in the DEFAULT-feature build. Add a shared helper (trait method, fn, const) whose only callers sit behind a default-off feature and CI stays green while 'cargo check --release' warns locally forever. No CI lane gates default-feature warnings. Rule: when adding a helper to a non-feature-gated module, check who calls it — if every caller is feature-gated, gate the declaration+impl too (#[cfg(feature = "x")]), and run BOTH 'cargo check --release' and clippy --all-features before committing.
invariant-file-move-rebaselines-citation: File splits/moves in native/angr/src/ re-red the baseline-audit gates (tools/check_line_citations.py and siblings): their baselines are keyed on <path>\t<comment-text>, so a line-number citation that was baselined under the OLD file reappears as a NEW violation under the new one, and the gate is only green again once you act on it. Preferred fix is to SYMBOL-ANCHOR the moved citation (cite the fn/struct it points at, per CLAUDE.md's symbol-anchor convention) and DELETE the old baseline row -- that shrinks the debt instead of relocating it. Repathing the row is the fallback when the target genuinely has no resolvable symbol; never reach for --update-baseline, which would silently re-add the row under the new path. Seen angr-c7xno.45 (expressions.rs -> expressions_inspect.rs) where two rows moved and both resolved to real Python symbols (SimSolver.Unconstrained, AddressConcretizationMixin._apply_concretization_strategies).
invariant-file-size-split-convention: File-size split convention for native/angr/src (established angr-a2br.2 context.rs split, angr-7hwz value.rs split; test-file ambiguity resolved by angr-5mnx3.49 commit 5a84a60a0): every file — PROD AND TEST ALIKE — stays under ~2000 lines. Test files are NOT exempt; angr-p3bi's close text mused the owner 'may rule test files exempt' but the repo's actual shape had already settled the other way (vex/ops/tests_vec_*.rs, symbolic/value_ops_property_tests.rs, symbolic/value_z3_fp_tests.rs are all one-topic-per-file siblings). The split recipe, in order: (1) cut along the section banners already in the file — they are the author's own topic boundaries and land on test boundaries; (2) give each new file a //! module doc naming its scope and cross-referencing its siblings; (3) register each with test_submod!(z3 "file.rs" => modname) from the PROD file (keeping the same z3 gate — see no-default-features-test-gating), NOT from mod.rs; (4) a helper used by MORE THAN ONE resulting module moves to a shared <base>_tests_support.rs as pub(super) — sibling test modules are all children of the same prod module, so super::<base>_tests_support::helper resolves; a helper used by exactly one stays private there. VERIFY the split lost nothing: grep -c the fn decls before and after (must match) and confirm cargo test --release reports the SAME pass count, not merely green. Then rename-sweep: moving a test between modules breaks doc citations of the form `module::test_name` — the value_tests split had 2 in-repo (value_ops_property_tests.rs) plus 7 bd memories to repair. PROD-side addendum (angr-5mnx3.1, arch/mod.rs -> register_file.rs + registry.rs): moving an `impl` block out of a mod.rs into a sibling breaks two things the type-checker only reports one at a time. (1) A method that was PRIVATE in the impl was visible to the `mod_tests.rs` sibling (both descendants of the same module); once the impl lives one level deeper it is not — widen exactly those to pub(super), not the whole impl. (2) An item that was DEFINED in mod.rs and is read only by tests (ArchDesc/ALL_ARCHES) becomes an `unused_imports` warning the moment it is re-exported instead, because the plain lib build has no consumer — CI clippy is --all-targets -D warnings, so it reds. Fix by making the sibling `pub(crate) mod` and having the tests path through it, keeping the re-export for the members lib code actually uses. (3) A type the moved code references ONLY in an intra-doc link (`[`SymContext`]` in a doc comment) must still be imported for rustdoc to resolve it, but rustc's unused_imports pass does NOT count doc-link uses — so the import warns and CI clippy -D warnings reds. Spell it `#[expect(unused_imports, reason = "referenced only by the intra-doc links below")]` rather than `allow`: if a later edit gives the import a real code use, unfulfilled_lint_expectations tells you to drop the attribute, whereas an `allow` would sit there forever. Seen in angr-fs8kb.35 (context.rs -> context_snapshot.rs / local_constraints.rs, both of which only name SymContext in prose). (4) angr-fs8kb.44 (sprintf.rs -> sprintf_spec.rs/sprintf_conv.rs, scanf.rs -> scanf_spec.rs): the `_tests.rs` sibling reaches the prod file's private items through `use super::*`, so ANY const/helper you move out of the prod file into a new sibling module breaks the test file even when the move is pure code motion and nothing changed visibility. rustc reports it as E0425 'cannot find value X in this scope' in the TEST file, pointing at the moved definition -- which reads like a visibility bug and is not; the fix is an explicit `use crate::<path>::<new_mod>::{X, y};` in the test file, plus pub(super) on the moved item. Corollary: do NOT keep the moved item imported in the prod file just to re-expose it to `super::*` -- with no lib-side consumer that is an unused_imports warning and CI clippy -D warnings reds, same trap as (2) above. (5) angr-fs8kb.20 (opcode_map.rs -> opcode_map_float.rs/opcode_map_vector.rs): when the prod file defines `macro_rules!` that the moved code invokes, textual macro scope does NOT follow the code to a SIBLING module (it covers only the defining module and its children), so each macro needs a `pub(super) use <name>;` line immediately after its definition and the new module imports it by path. Second half of the same trap: macro bodies name types unqualified (IROp/IRType/FCmpKind here) and macro_rules paths resolve at the CALL site, so the correct import list for each new module is whatever ITS OWN invocations expand to -- not a copy of the parent's `use` line. Expect the parent to shed an import as a result (FCmpKind became unused in opcode_map.rs once the fcmp_* invocations left), which CI clippy -D warnings will red. Verification for a macro-heavy split: grep -c the macro invocations (`_arms!`) as well as the fn decls before and after. (6) angr-fs8kb.66 (expressions.rs -> expressions_loads.rs/expressions_arith.rs): a baseline-gated audit script (tools/audit_silent_fallback.py and its four siblings) keys each known site by RELATIVE PATH, so moving a baselined line into a new file makes the gate report it as a NEW untagged site -- with the old entry now orphaned and silently unenforced. Fix by editing the one path in the baseline .txt (keeping its sorted position), NOT by --update-baseline, which would re-accept every other drift in the same run. Same reasoning as the pinned-baseline rule in run_regression.py: a refresh command hides the diff a hand edit makes reviewable. (7) angr-fs8kb.96 (statements_tests.rs -> statements_dirty_tests.rs/statements_cas_tests.rs): rule (4)'s `super::<base>_tests_support::helper resolves` claim holds ONLY while every test module is registered from the SAME prod file. When the split is PER PROD SIBLING -- each test module registered from the file it covers, which is the shape rule (3) pushes you toward once the prod side is already split -- the consumers are children of DIFFERENT prod modules and no `super::` path reaches across them. Register the support module one level up, from the package's mod.rs, and have each test module import it by full crate path (`use crate::interpreter::statements_tests_support::{..};`). `pub(super)` on the helpers is still the right visibility: super is now the package module, so it scopes them to exactly the subtree that may use them, without widening to pub(crate). This is the one sanctioned exception to rule (3)'s register-from-the-prod-file-not-mod.rs -- and it applies to the SUPPORT module only; the test modules themselves still register from their own prod sibling.
invariant-find-avoid-routing-is-find-fir: invariant: find/avoid routing is FIND-FIRST at every site (angr-03vl4.14). A pc in both find_addrs and avoid_addrs goes to FOUND, never AVOID — angr's Python Explorer documents that as the default (avoid_priority=False, angr/exploration_techniques/explorer.py::_filter_inner) and the Rust engine exposes no avoid_priority knob at all. set_find_addrs/set_avoid_addrs never reject an overlap, so it IS a reachable config. Five routing sites must agree or the same state routes differently depending on which side of a step boundary it is observed on (and, for the worker, on RUST_PARALLEL_WORKERS): run_loop_single.rs::step_one (pre-step, both find arms — needs_python predicate then addrs — before both avoid arms), helpers.rs::route_successor (fresh successors), step_one's SimProcedure-bounce arm (is_find = find_addrs.contains(addr), else AVOID), run_loop_wave.rs's bounce_target_addr match, and run_loop_worker.rs::parallel_process_state. Any NEW routing site must be find-first too. Regression pinned by run_loop_single_tests.rs::pre_step_and_post_step_routing_agree_on_an_overlapping_address, which drives one config through step_one AND route_successor and asserts the same stash.
invariant-find-state-mut-covers-pending: RustExplorationManager::find_state / find_state_mut (exploration/helpers.rs) search all THREE live-state buckets, in this precedence order: pending_callbacks (hash lookup) -> the stashes -> pending_parallel_bounces (linear scan, added angr-eukuf). (2) The parked-bounce leg MUST stay last: an id can be resident in a stash AND parked at once, and flush_parked_bounces_to_active drops the parked copy as the redundant duplicate in exactly that case, so the stash copy is the one carrying the path forward and must win the lookup too. (3) find_state_mut cannot use a &mut self bucket method for that leg — the receiver conflicts with the pending_callbacks borrow the early return holds for the whole fn. That is why the bucket bodies are pub(super) FREE functions over the field (run_loop::parked_states_mut etc., angr-0jh0j.82): find_state_mut calls run_loop::parked_states_mut(&mut self.pending_parallel_bounces) and keeps the disjoint-field borrow. Two instances found in round 7: scanf's numeric arm (%d/%u/%x/%o) dropped field_width, minting a free full-width BVS where Python's FormatString.interpret range-constrains to [-(base**(d-1)-1), base**d - 1] whenever d*log2(base) < bits — fixed by scanf_spec.rs::digit_range_bound + ScanfSpec.digit_bound (angr-6cp06.9); and sprintf's '.*' precision consuming a vararg unconditionally (angr-6cp06.8). RULE when adding/editing a specifier arm: read the matching branch of format_parser.py::FormatString.interpret (packets path) and .replace/.interpret (addr path) and account for EVERY component field it reads (length_spec, pad_chr, size, spec_type) — an unused parsed field is the bug signature. Prefer computing the derived bound at parse time as a pure fn (testable without z3, so the four --no-default-features combos keep coverage) over inlining it in do_scanf.
invariant-fp-return-register: FP-return calling convention: CallingConvention::fp_return_register() (native/angr/src/arch/calling_conventions.rs) is the single source of truth for where a scalar double return lands. Some(224)=xmm0 on SystemVAMD64, Some(320)=q0/v0 on AArch64, None everywhere else. The None reasons differ: x86 returns in the x87 st0 stack and ARM EABI soft-float in the r0:r1 integer pair (neither modelled); MIPS O32/N64 DO expose the register (mips32_off::F0/mips64_off::F0, aliased f0/$f0 in ALIASES_MIPS32/64) — the blocker is float-ABI-variant ambiguity, since a hard-float MIPS binary returns the double in $f0 but a -msoft-float build returns it in the $v0/$v1 integer pair and nothing in a RegisterFile distinguishes them. Same ambiguity that keeps MipsO32::fp_arg_registers deliberately empty. (Corrected angr-sqfj8.9: the older 'our register files do not expose $f0 yet' claim was false.) A native proc returning a double writes the 64-bit IEEE-754 bit pattern to the LOW 64 bits of that offset and must return Ok(None) to suppress the dispatcher's default integer-return store (see procedures/strtod.rs::NativeStrtod). To add a new FP-return arch: implement the trait method, do NOT hard-code an offset in the proc. Companion: cc_for_arch() is the non-panicking registry lookup — use it in procs that can defer to Python; default_cc_for_arch() keeps the loud panic for argument extraction, where a wrong CC would silently yield wrong-but-plausible args.
invariant-fp-test-witnesses: Writing FP tests for the Rust engine: three traps that silently make a test vacuous or flaky. (1) 1/3 is NOT a valid RNE-vs-RZ rounding witness — its binary expansion rounds DOWN, so round-nearest and round-toward-zero produce identical bits, and an rm-threading test built on it passes even when the rounding mode is dropped entirely (the angr-c7xno.85 bug shape). Use 0.1 (rounds up into a double) or sqrt(2); scaling a witness by a power of two does NOT change its rounding direction, so 2/3 is just as useless as 1/3. Assert BOTH 'RZ != RNE' and 'RZ == RNE - 1' so the witness proves itself. (2) NEVER assert the exact bit pattern of a NaN *result* coming out of the symbolic path: symbolic/value_z3.rs::float_to_ieee_bv uses Z3_mk_fpa_to_ieee_bv, which Z3 leaves UNSPECIFIED for NaN, so the model may hand back any bits (including a finite value) and the assertion is nondeterministic. Ask the FP theory instead — FloatOpKind::IsNaN over the operand — and note that round-tripping a NaN through the ieee-bv encoding and back into a Float is equally unspecified, so IsNaN over an ieee-bv-encoded intermediate does not rescue it. Infinities are safe: they have unique IEEE encodings. (3) When you constrain a SYMBOLIC operand and assert the solved value, a unique encoding of the RESULT does not pin the OPERAND — rounding collapses a whole interval of operands onto one result, so 'assert_eq!(eval_f64(&ctx, &x), 2.5)' for 'x + 1.5 == 4.0' asserts a Z3 model preference, not a semantic fact (angr-63g3w: RNE's solution set is {2.5, 2.5 + 1 ULP}, since the latter's exact sum is a tie that rounds down because 4.0's significand is even). Compute the true solution set by hand FIRST; then assert (a) the returned model satisfies the constraint under Rust's own concrete add, and (b) the solution set itself, one pinned candidate per is_sat() call — that second form is strictly stronger AND doubles as a rounding-mode check, because a wrong mode admits/rejects different neighbours. See native/angr/src/symbolic/value_z3_fp_tests.rs::test_fp_add_symbolic_solution_set_is_exactly_rne and its sibling test_fp_add_with_symbolic_operand_solves, whose comments carry all three rationales at the assertions.
invariant-fs-gate-polarity-serve-vs-mint: INVARIANT for native stdio/read procs (native/angr/src/procedures/): the FileSystem::is_open gate has TWO polarities and picking the wrong one is silently wrong. A proc that SERVES content natively (read.rs, fread.rs) bounces to Python on the UNTRACKED fd — Python's SimFile model owns bytes Rust cannot see. A proc that MINTS fresh unconstrained BVs instead of parsing content (do_fscanf in scanf.rs; the same shape as NativeSscanf's whole-call deferral) must bounce on the TRACKED/open fd — over real content a free BVS makes impossible paths feasible and never advances FileDescriptor::position, so a later native read/fread re-reads bytes the mint conceptually consumed. Key on is_open, not fd_info().is_some(): a closed fd has no live cursor to corrupt. The tracked-fd bounce is coherent because rust_callback_dispatch::_inject_rust_fds hydrates the callback state's posix.fd from the Rust descriptor (name, content, position). Ask which polarity a new proc needs before copying a sibling's gate.
invariant-global-counter-test-delta-not-: Process-global-counter tests must assert on a DELTA across their own bump window, never on an absolute threshold over the whole emitted map. angr-c0wlh: test_simplify_sample_ticker_is_not_emitted (native/angr/src/symbolic/stats_tests.rs) scanned get_solver_stats() for any value >= MARK (1<<40), which conflates its own marker with any unrelated large counter, and needed a name-based contains('time')/ends_with('_ns') carve-out for wall-clock sums — a duration counter spelled any other way slips through. Fix: snapshot before + after the bump, flag only keys that grew by >= MARK, with saturating_sub so a concurrent reset_solver_stats() reads as no-growth (fails safe: a reset can hide a real leak, never invent one). Same rule applies to total_while_bumped's siblings. Also: MARK-bump helpers must call undo_bump BEFORE any assert/expect that can panic, or the marker leaks into the global counter for the rest of the process.
invariant-guest-size-host-allocation-cap: Guest-controlled size/offset feeding a HOST allocation must be capped natively in the Rust handler — do NOT 'fall back to Python' as the defense. The Python procedure (e.g. procedures/posix/mmap.py -> map_region, brk.py -> set_brk) allocates just as eagerly, so bouncing only relocates the OOM. Rust's SymbolicMemory::map walks the range page-by-page and MemoryPage::new does an eager `vec![0u8; PAGE_SIZE]` per page (NOT lazy/COW from a shared zero page), so an unbounded length also hangs the O(pages) scan long before it OOMs. Five shared caps: syscalls::mod's MAX_IO_SIZE (bytes serviced natively before a legitimate Python fallback) and MAX_MAP_SIZE (host-safety bound on address space MAPPED; used by syscalls::mmap::do_mmap as MAX_MMAP_SIZE and syscalls::brk::NativeBrkSyscall::call as MAX_BRK_GROWTH), state::filesystem::fd's MAX_FS_FILE_SIZE (host-safety bound on an fd's eager content Vec; enforced inside FileSystem::write / write_at, angr-c7xno.67) and MAX_FD (upper bound on a caller-chosen fd number; enforced inside FileSystem::dup2, angr-03vl4.52), plus procedures::malloc's MAX_ALLOC_SIZE (every allocator proc — malloc/calloc/realloc/memalign/posix_memalign — calls check_max with it before state.heap_alloc). Note the destination-vs-length distinction that hid .67: MAX_IO_SIZE bounds only the per-call LENGTH at every call site, never the write OFFSET, so an unbounded lseek/pwrite64 offset still reached resize(). Reject the way the real kernel signals failure — mmap returns -1/MAP_FAILED, brk returns the UNCHANGED break — rather than erroring out. ORDERING RULE (angr-c7xno.67): when a host-safety refusal lives at a choke point that also performs an ownership transfer (FileSystem::write's demote_symbolic_content, which hands a registered file to Python), the refusal must come AFTER the transfer — refusing first leaves Rust serving stale native content while the Python fallback performs the write. Place it before any Arc::make_mut so a refusal costs no CoW. LAYERING RULE (angr-03vl4.52): the cap belongs on the shared MODEL method, not on one entry point. Most libc calls have TWO native entry points into the same model — the raw syscall handler (syscalls/) and the libc SimProcedure (procedures/) — and a bound enforced in only one is simply absent from the other: syscalls::file_descriptor::dup2_body enforced NEWFD_LIMIT while procedures::fileops::NativeDup2 called the identical FileSystem::dup2 with no bound at all. When Python-parity ordering forces a duplicate check at the entry point (Python's dup2 returns success for oldfd==newfd BEFORE its range test), keep the entry-point check but derive its constant from the model's, never a second literal. Corollary: a guest fd/handle arrives as u64; narrowing it with `as u32` at the entry point ALIASES an unrelated object (0x1_0000_0000 -> 0 == stdin), so use u32::try_from and treat overflow as the not-found error. NO-HOST-ALLOCATION COROLLARY (angr-03vl4.53): a cap is still required where the guest size drives NO host allocation at all. RustSimState::heap_alloc is pure address-space bookkeeping, yet an uncapped near-u64::MAX size wrapped its 16-byte rounding down to a tiny bump, so two logically-distinct mallocs ALIAS — a wrong symbolic-execution answer, not an OOM. So audit an allocator/IO family for SIBLING PARITY (four of five malloc procs capped; malloc alone did not) and make the shared model's size rounding saturating (state::process::round_alloc_size), not plain `+`. Keep Python-parity constants (syscalls::cgc::CGC_MAX_ALLOCATION mirrors state.cgc.max_allocation) separate from host-safety caps even when the value coincides, so lowering one for safety can't silently break parity.
invariant-guest-state-size-vs-archinfo: MIPS32/MIPS64 GUEST_STATE_SIZE in arch/mips.rs (offsets32/offsets64) used to be 432/592 -- exactly where the late-VEX bookkeeping block (emnote/cmstart/cmlen/nraddr/...ip_at_syscall) BEGINS, so the guest state buffer truncated every register archinfo places after the FPU control block. angr-9ke6b.10 grew them to archinfo's real state end (496/624). Convention across arch/: GUEST_STATE_SIZE == max(offset+size) over archinfo's register map (X86 344, AMD64 1060, MIPS32 496, MIPS64 624; ARM 400 is 4 over archinfo's 396). RegisterFile::new allocates vec![0u8; arch.state_size()], and arch/registry_tests.rs::register_names_all_resolve_and_fit_in_u128 + vex_bookkeeping_fields_resolve_on_every_arch both assert offset+size <= state_size, so a new register past the old bound fails loudly rather than corrupting. PLACEMENT RULE: emnote/cmstart/cmlen/nraddr/ip_at_syscall live in each arch's ALIASES table, not CANONICAL (so register_name reverse lookup does not claim those offsets) and not REGISTER_NAMES (not exported to Python's named-register channel) -- X86/ARM/ARM64 set that precedent and AMD64/MIPS now match.
invariant-icicle-behind-fuzzer-feature: icicle.rs lives at native/angr/src/fuzzer/icicle.rs (moved there from the crate root in angr-fs8kb.85) and is behind the default-OFF `fuzzer` cargo feature — fuzzer.rs declares `pub(crate) mod icicle;` under lib.rs's #[cfg(feature = "fuzzer")] gate on `mod fuzzer`. invariant-ieee-maxnum-not-rust-f32-max: Rust's `f32::max`/`f64::max` (and `min`) are NOT a drop-in for IEEE-754-2008 maxNum/minNum in VEX ops: they lower to LLVM `maxnum`, whose docs leave the ±0 case as 'may return either operand', while ARM's FPMax/FPMin — which VMAXNM/VMINNM (`Iop_MaxNumF32/64`, `Iop_MinNumF32/64`) defer to once NaNs are handled — pin maxNum(+0,-0)=+0 and minNum(+0,-0)=-0. Spell the concrete path out by hand: NaN operands first (return the *other* one — that is what makes it maxNum rather than max), then the `-0.0 == 0.0` tie, then the ordered compare. See `num_min_max` in `vex/ops/float_arith.rs`. Note also that the compare-and-select `FMin`/`FMax` lane ops in `vex/ops/lane_traits.rs` are a *different* op family with deliberately different NaN behaviour (SSE MINPS/MAXPS style: whichever operand the compare falls through to) — do not unify them. Symbolic side is fine: SMT-LIB `fp.max`/`fp.min` (Z3_mk_fpa_max/min) already carry the maxNum NaN contract and are exact, so no rounding mode is threaded. Sibling of invariant-rust-as-cast-is-rne-only.
invariant-init-cache-plugin-coverage: INVARIANT: the Rust manager's init cache (rust_disk_cache.py + rust_manager._try_in_memory_init_cache/_try_disk_init_cache) is built from a plain blank_state and re-attached to a user state via _apply_state_metadata, which ONLY carries constraints, globals, and an option allow-list. The allow-list is ALSO a mirror (add when src has it, discard when it doesn't): options not listed get STRIPPED on init-cache hits, and listed options must be mirror-applied (not just additive) because the in-memory _init_cache is keyed by binary path — a cached state populated from a prior STRICT_PAGE_ACCESS run would otherwise leak that option to a subsequent caller that didn't request it. Mirror pattern introduced commit 1c3263198 (angr-zd4x); TRACK_ACTION_HISTORY added for preconstrainer compat in angr-fkvt (2026-06-06). Read the tuple in _apply_state_metadata for the live list (LAZY_SOLVES, STRICT_PAGE_ACCESS, ENABLE_NX, NO_IP_CONCRETIZATION, NO_SYMBOLIC_JUMP_RESOLUTION, KEEP_IP_SYMBOLIC, TRACK_ACTION_HISTORY, plus _NATIVE_SIMOPTIONS since angr-kzjv6) — when adding a new honored SimOption you MUST add it there or the option silently disappears after the first cache-warm run. The cache does NOT carry memory pages, the fs (SimFilesystem) plugin, or the posix fd table. Therefore any user state customization beyond constraints/globals/allow-listed options must be detected by _state_has_user_symbolic (the cache-disable gate) — otherwise a cache hit silently drops it. As of commit 00a1bb3dc the gate scans: SP stack page, non-stack symbolic memory pages, register file, AND state.fs._files (non-empty => disable). The gate is enforced in _compute_disk_init_key (and _compute_mem_init_key): returns '' when the state has user-created symbolic data (e.g. argv BVS — blank_state from cache cannot round-trip their identity), suppressing BOTH the load AND save paths. If you add a new user-customizable plugin that must survive init, EITHER extend _apply_state_metadata to copy it OR extend _state_has_user_symbolic to disable the cache when it is populated. Tests: tests/engines/rust/test_state_roundtrip.py::TestInitCacheUserSymbolicGate. || THIRD FAILURE MODE, added angr-6cp06.12 (2026-09-07): a CONCRETE plugin scalar is caught by NEITHER lever. _state_has_user_symbolic only gates on symbolic data, and _apply_state_metadata does not copy plugin attributes, so simos/linux.py's state.posix.{argv,argc,environ,auxv} pointers were all None after _deserialize_init_state even though the KEY=VALUE string table they point at IS in the cached stack_page. As of angr-7tmoz all four are persisted and restored: the three address-shaped ones through _extract_posix_pointer over the _POSIX_POINTER_FIELDS tuple, argc through _extract_posix_argc as a (value, width) pair because consumers call BV methods on it (argc.sign_extend), and all of them re-attached as claripy BVs by _restore_posix_entry_fields (_PYTHON_METADATA_VERSION now 3). GENERAL RULE: any Rust<->Python bridge that reads a plugin attribute at state-add time must ALSO persist it in the pickle, or it works cold and silently no-ops warm. TESTING GOTCHA: such a bug is invisible to a fresh-checkout test run — a cold cache takes the real Python-init path and passes. Force the disk path explicitly (construct one manager to populate, RustExplorationManager._init_cache.clear(), construct a second) as tests/engines/rust/test_environ_seed.py::test_warm_disk_cache_hit_keeps_environ does; a single-run green here proves nothing. SECOND TESTING GOTCHA (angr-7tmoz): a warm-disk test that uses the real ~/.cache/angr_rust_init is order-dependent — a pickle a prior run left behind means the cold run never calls _save_init_to_disk_cache, so a capture-the-save fixture skips instead of failing. Redirect _disk_cache_dir at a tmp_path, and do it with mock.patch.object, NOT a setattr/restore pair: the mixin defines it as an inherited staticmethod, so restoring by hand rebinds a plain function onto the class that then eats self and breaks disk caching for every later test in the session (464 failures, all green in isolation). See tests/engines/rust/test_disk_cache_posix.py.

invariant-leak-gate-must-prove-it-can-fa: Leak-gate self-test caught a bug in the GATE, not the engine (angr-c4xcs.4). A deliberate leak injector written as std::mem::forget(Box::new([0u8;64])) is ELIDED ENTIRELY by release-mode LLVM: the allocation is never read and never dropped, so it is dead code. Result: valgrind saw nothing, the self-test reported clean, and the leak gate was silently incapable of failing. Fix: Box::into_raw(vec![0u8;64].into_boxed_slice()) + std::hint::black_box(ptr) -- opaque to the optimizer, unreachable to memcheck, so it lands in 'definitely lost'. Now measures exactly 64.00 B/iter. See inject_leak() in native/angr/examples/leak_probe.rs. INVARIANT (generalized in angr-91vj9.7): any gate that can only report 'clean' -- leak, perf, or a baseline-gated LINT -- must ship a self-test that proves it can fail, and that self-test must run BEFORE the real check in CI. nightly-ci.yml::valgrind_leak_check and ci.yml's 'VEX rounding-mode threading audit' both do this; the latter's self_test() in tools/audit_rounding_mode_threading.py classifies a synthetic threaded/dropped-underscore/dropped-unused/exempt quartet, which matters most for a lint whose baseline is EMPTY -- it then passes vacuously on day one and nothing distinguishes 'no violations' from 'detector broken'.
invariant-legacy-stat-numbers-unregister: Legacy (pre-LFS) stat-family syscall numbers must stay UNREGISTERED in the Rust native registry on every 32-bit arch: i386/ARM 106/107/108, MIPS32 4106/4107/4108. Older comments claiming 'angr's i386/arm maps have no legacy entry' were false — the correct rationale is the layout mismatch. mod_tests.rs::file_path_stubs_registered_on_all_arches now asserts all nine are absent.
invariant-lineage-flag-propagation: SymContext per-lineage flags (deterministic, use_shared_lineage_solver) are inherited by fork() so a whole diamond stays in one witness-selection mode. with_timeout() hardcodes BOTH to false. Any code that builds a SymContext via with_timeout/new and represents a continuation of an existing lineage MUST re-propagate these flags. Known sites that must: merge() (snapshot_fork_ops.rs, OR across all input arms) and to_snapshot/restore_from_snapshot (SymContextSnapshot carries them as serde-default fields, angr-ph300.46). Missing propagation silently reverts deterministic eval to arbitrary-Z3 witnesses -> run-to-run nondeterminism returns at the merge/restore point with no error. invariant-local-constraints-struct: native/angr/src/symbolic/local_constraints.rs (split out of context.rs by angr-fs8kb.35) holds a pub(super) LocalConstraints struct that combines both assumed (Vec<(RustBV, bool)>) and z3_assertions (Vec<z3::ast::Bool>, gated on vex-engine-z3) under one Mutex<LocalConstraints> field on SymContext. This replaced the prior two separate Mutex<Vec<...>> fields (assumed_constraints_local + z3_assertions_local). Why: hot path (assume_true/assume_false/add_constraint_raw) used to acquire 2 locks per call; now 1. How to apply: when adding new assumed/z3_assertion writes, lock once via self.local_constraints.lock() and access fields via .assumed and .z3_assertions. Reads should follow the same pattern; never reintroduce separate Mutexes for these two vectors. The shared Arc<Vec<...>> prefixes (assumed_constraints_shared / z3_assertions_shared) remain as separate fields -- only the local additions are combined. Fork-time freeze: snapshot_fork_ops.rs::freeze_into_shared<T: Clone> is the generic helper that replaced the prior two specialized fns (freeze_z3_assertions, freeze_assumed_constraints). It takes a &Mutex<Arc<Vec<T>>> shared prefix plus a &mut Vec<T> local -- the caller already holds the LocalConstraints lock and passes a mutable ref to the field. This avoids a redundant lock/unlock cycle inside fork() and lets fork freeze both vectors under one local-lock acquisition. Never re-introduce per-vector freeze fns or have freeze acquire the local Mutex itself -- SymContext::fork/merge (z3 and non-z3 paths) are the only callers, and they lock LocalConstraints once and pass &mut local.assumed and &mut local.z3_assertions. Cloning-vs-moving discipline: with scope_open=true (an open bare push/pop scope, i.e. bare_local_savepoints non-empty) freeze always clones, because the matching pop() must be able to truncate local; otherwise Arc::get_mut+append moves elements without per-element clones.
invariant-log-warn-not-observable-in-tes: Rust tests cannot observe a log::warn! emission in this test binary, and must not try to count its arguments either. So 'assert_eq!(calls, 1)' on a lazily-built log argument is wrong by construction; only the upper bound ('<= 1', i.e. never twice) is assertable, and that is the half a dedup-latch regression would break anyway. Applies to every SILENT(cat-b)/(cat-c) site whose tag mandates a log::warn!: test the latch/atomic or the predicate the warning reports on, never the emission.

invariant-max-active-states-two-sites: max_active_states enforcement has TWO sites, not one. Serial: RustExplorationManager::push_to_active_or_drop (exploration/helpers.rs) against sm.active_count(). Since angr-5mnx3.18 the admission is RESERVED with a compare_exchange loop (worker::reserve_admission), not decided from a plain load and fetch_add-ed afterwards: the old check-then-act let W workers each spend the same stale pending snapshot, so the bound was soft by a MULTIPLE of the worker count, not the documented workers-1. invariant-memoryerror-variant-dispositio: INVARIANT: adding a MemoryError variant (native/angr/src/memory/mod.rs) requires triaging its disposition at the interpreter's two dispatch matches — VEXInterpreter::try_rust_memory_load (expressions_loads.rs) and try_rust_memory_store (statements_store.rs). Both end in a catch-all 'Err(e) => Err(CbExecutionError::Memory(e))', and CbExecutionError::Memory maps to FallbackStrategy::Panic (execution_error.rs::strategy), so a new variant is TERMINAL by default — it errors the whole state instead of degrading to Ok(None)/Ok(false) like Unmapped/UnmappedPageInRegion/SymbolicAddress. MemoryError is #[non_exhaustive], so the wildcard is required and the compiler cannot force the decision (unlike CbExecutionError::strategy, which is wildcard-free). invariant-merge-config-field-classes: RustSimState::merge (state/fork.rs) config-field policy, settled by angr-9ke6b.121: every field a native proc or Python setter can mutate AFTER a fork needs an explicit merge rule, not a self-only carry. Three classes: (1) set-like -> union: hooks and sim_options via the union_arc_set helper (returns self's Arc untouched when all branches are Arc::ptr_eq, so the no-divergence case allocates nothing), environment via a HashMap union with earlier-branch-wins + warn on a conflicting VALUE (mirrors union_overlay). (2) sim-option boolean mirrors (no_ip_concretization, no_symbolic_jump_resolution, keep_ip_symbolic, force_eager_forks) -> logical OR, because they are a second view of the sim_options set that is unioned; self-only carry would revert a branch's set_option. (3) per-path cursors and init-time config with no meaningful union (getopt_optind/optchar, getopt_extern, ctype_loc, concretizer, inspection enabled_mask) -> keep self's value but call warn_config_divergence, the same loud-drop contract the fs longest-stdout merge uses. When adding a new RustSimState field, put it in one of these three classes; the audit found the whole config block was silently in an unstated fourth class. AddressConcretizer/CtypeLocPtrs/GetoptExternAddrs carry PartialEq solely for the class-3 checks. EXTENSION (angr-fs8kb.71): class 3 is not only for scalars — it is where any per-path STACK belongs too. native_resume_stack (angr-sqfj8.86) and call_stack both carry warn_on_diverge + #[merge_manual] with a hand-written *_diverges fn in fork.rs, because a silently dropped branch's frames corrupt that path's return flow with no diagnostic, and because the mechanical !=-based body does not fit. Two reasons it does not fit, and they generalize to any future class-3 aggregate: (a) an element type may have no usable PartialEq (NativeResumeFrame holds RustBVs whose PartialEq is documented non-reflexive for symbolic values), and (b) an element may carry per-path NOISE that must be excluded or the warning fires on every merge and says nothing (CallStackEntry::stack_ptr — two branches reconverging at one pc legitimately recorded different SPs at the same call site; call_stack_diverges compares only depth + the call_site/callee/return triple, which is what interpreter::exits' is_ret/is_empty arm actually reads). The same noise argument is why merge's inspection check is scoped to 'enabled_mask only'. Reachability note worth keeping: the default Python-facing RustExplorationManager.merge() groups candidates by PROGRAM COUNTER alone (_merge_native in angr/exploration/rust_manager.py), not by call stack, so a cross-call-history merge is the ordinary case, not a misuse.
invariant-merge-inputs-use-clone-for-mer: Copying a RustSimState for a *merge input* must use RustSimState::clone_for_merge, never fork(). fork() intentionally resets the three removal-tombstone sets (removed_hooks / removed_sim_options / removed_env_keys) because a child has removed nothing relative to itself yet — but RustSimState::merge subtracts exactly those sets to keep one branch's remove_hook/set_option(_,false)/unsetenv from being resurrected by a sibling. Forking before merging therefore silently defeats the angr-9ke6b.121 tombstone fix. That is exactly what _merge_states (exploration/state_lifecycle.rs) did until angr-sqfj8.33: RustSimState::merge was correct but nothing reached it with tombstones intact, so the whole manager-level / register_merge_point path resurrected removals. Generalization: when a unit test covers a low-level primitive directly, check that the production entry point does not pre-process its inputs in a way that neuters the invariant — add the test at the entry point too.
invariant-merge-overlay-earlier-wins: RustSimState::merge (native/angr/src/state/fork.rs::merge) resolves overlay-map key conflicts by earlier-wins iteration order: self > earlier-other > later-other. All three overlay maps (symbolic_pages, hook_symbolic_memory, addr_to_ast) share the identical union loop that only inserts a key if !contains_key, so the FIRST branch to own a key wins. A 2-state test cannot distinguish this from later-wins; needs >=3 states where a conflicting key lives in two DIFFERENT others but not self. Covered by state/tests/merge_multi_state.rs::test_merge_three_state_overlay_union_and_tiebreak (angr-qwyti.2/n0irt.18): tag entries by provenance (size field for hook/addr_to_ast, int AST value for symbolic_pages) so a reversed others fold flips the merged tag and fails. stdin_symbols unions with dedup-by-name, self-order-first.
invariant-mips-syscall-error-reg: MIPS Linux syscalls report error in $a3 (0=ok, non-zero=err) separately from $v0 return; glibc branches on it. Rust dispatcher must mirror angr's linux_syscall_update_error_reg: when unsigned ret >= SYSCALL_ERRNO_START (-1133 for both O32/N64), set error_reg=all-ones and ret=-ret (positive errno); else error_reg=0, ret passthrough. $a3 VEX offsets: 36 (MIPS32, base 8 + 7*4), 72 (MIPS64, base 16 + 7*8). Implemented via CallingConvention::syscall_error_register()->Option<(offset, errno_start)> in arch/calling_conventions.rs + CcSnapshot::write_syscall_return() in exploration/core_outcome_cc.rs (angr-pfbu; the fn moved out of stepping.rs with the angr-nbim4.3 post-step-core split). Pinned since angr-5mnx3.4 by calling_conventions_tests::test_syscall_error_register_only_on_mips_and_names_a3 (the tuple: $a3 by name on MIPS, None everywhere else) and core_outcome_tests/syscall_dispatch.rs::write_syscall_return_splits_errno_flag_into_a3_on_mips (the behaviour, incl. the inclusive errno_start boundary) plus its _passes_through_on_abis_without_an_error_register control.
invariant-mirror-pair-hardening-sweep: MIRROR-PAIR SWEEP RULE (angr-5mnx3.67): when a fix hardens one member of a documented mirror pair, apply it to every sibling in the SAME commit and re-read the shared parent module's doc. Found instance: angr-j60q0.2 hardened VEXOps::vec_float_lane_op's over-arity debug_assert! into OpError::UnsupportedVectorOp; the sibling VEXOps::vec_int_lane_op (vex/ops/vec_int_lane.rs, whose own module doc says 'Mirrors ops/vec_float_lane.rs for the integer family') landed the same day and kept the debug_assert!, leaving a release-mode buf[idx] OOB process abort for any future IntLaneOp with arity() > INT_LANE_OP_MAX_ARITY. invariant-mirror-pattern: Mirror pattern for cross-mixin invariants in Rust rustdoc (angr-a2br.1.5, 2026-06-01; citations repaired angr-9ke6b.122, 2026-08-03): when the source-of-truth contract lives in a Python module docstring (the 'Cross-mixin invariants' section of angr/exploration/rust_manager.py's module docstring documents I1-I8), the Rust mirror at state/mod.rs, stash.rs and exploration/run_loop.rs should: (1) add a module-level rustdoc section listing all invariants with their Rust manifestation (or 'Python-only' tag for orchestration-only invariants — don't pretend Rust enforces them when it doesn't); (2) cross-reference from each Rust enforcement site back to the module-level summary AND back to the Python source — cite the docstring SECTION/invariant HEADING ('I8. Exploration-loop termination conditions'), never a raw rust_manager.py:NNN, which drifts: all three mirrors had rotted by 2026-08-03 (state/mod.rs :10-100 for a 10-134 docstring, run_loop.rs :98 for I8, stash.rs :74 for I6); (3) cite the matching regression test name verbatim (TestMmapBaseSync.test_export_path_..., TestStateCacheSizeBound.test_cleanup_state_cache_...) so a future reader can locate it. Corollary: the Python header has SEVERAL Rust citers, so fixing one stale citation means grepping 'rust_manager.py:' across native/ + docs/ and fixing the siblings in the same commit. Debug_asserts are 'where runtime-expressible' — many cross-language invariants aren't (e.g. I7 max() direction is enforced at the Python export site, not Rust). Use them sparingly for genuinely Rust-internal contracts (state_index/state_roots consistency in stash.rs, register size>0 in state/pymethods.rs::set_registers_bulk). Acceptance: cargo doc --no-deps clean, all tests pass.
invariant-mirror-python-semantics-not-ha: When a Rust VEX op/ccall disagrees with real hardware but AGREES with angr's Python engine, the correct outcome is to MIRROR PYTHON and document it — not to fix the Rust side. The two engines interleave within a single exploration (a block can fall back to Python mid-run), so a Rust-only correction makes the answer depend on which engine ran the block; a genuine fix is an upstream angr change that must land on both sides at once. Now seen in two unrelated subsystems: (1) arm64g ADC/SBC carry keyed off cc_dep2 instead of cc_dep3 — see invariant-arm64g-ccall-python-quirk; (2) vec_shift_vec (vex/ops/vec_shift.rs) reading the NEON shift-by-vector amount as UNSIGNED, where libVEX's own header FIXME says ARM32 means it signed (angr-0jh0j.64). VERIFICATION METHOD for this bug shape, both halves cheap: (a) what the front end really emits — .venv/bin/python -c 'import pyvex, archinfo; pyvex.lift(bytes, addr, archinfo.ArchARMEL(), opt_level=0).pp()' on a hand-encoded instruction; ARM32 vshl.s8 lifts to Sar8x8(v, Sub8x8(0, amt)), which is only coherent if a negative count means shift-left; (b) what Python computes — read angr/engines/vex/claripy/irop.py (_op_vector_mapped / _op_mapped / operation_map for the shift+arith+bitwise families). Close such a bead with the evidence plus a differential test pinning the agreement, and a REOPEN criterion naming the upstream change that would break it.
invariant-module-split-test-file-boundar: Splitting a big Rust module in this crate: the sibling <mod>_tests.rs file must be split along the SAME boundaries, and its section-comment markers are NOT trustworthy boundaries. In helpers_tests.rs (angr-9ke6b.76) the '// --- Timeout / LengthLimiter / LoopBound ---' banner covered ~460 lines that also contained the effective_pc tests and the whole materialize_deferred_forks block; slicing on the banners produced dangling doc comments ('error: expected item after doc comment') and cross-file fixture references. Reliable method: (1) list every top-level 'fn ' with line numbers and classify each by the symbol it exercises, not by the banner above it; (2) walk BACKWARD from each fn over contiguous ///, //, and #[..] lines to find the true block start; (3) after cutting, grep each new file's head/tail for a trailing doc comment or a leading orphaned fixture. Shared test fixtures (e.g. push_active_at) do not survive the split -- either move them with their only consumer or inline the one-off call; a #[cfg(test)] mod tests is private, so cross-module fixture sharing is not available without making the tests mod pub(crate). REGISTRATION (angr-12jjk.16): do NOT hand-write the old '#[cfg(test)] #[path=..] #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, reason=..)] mod x;' block -- since fe99f2553 every one of the ~117 sites goes through the crate-root 'test_submod!' macro_rules in lib.rs. Arms: test_submod!("file_tests.rs" => name) / test_submod!(name) for default file naming / a 'z3 ' prefix on either for the cfg(all(test, feature="vex-engine-z3")) gate. It is defined ahead of lib.rs's mod declarations so legacy textual macro scope reaches every module -- invoke it unqualified, and #[path] resolves relative to the INVOKING file (verified by the full cargo test --all-targets build). DOC DUPLICATION (angr-5mnx3.69): the extraction also leaves TWO copies of the submodule's op-set description — a doc comment on the 'mod X;' decl in the parent, and the file's own '//!' header — and a later move of individual ops between submodules updates only the file header. In vex/ops/mod.rs three decl comments (vec_int_arith, vec_compare, vec_permute_mul) still named families that had since migrated to the vec_int_lane_op driver, or omitted families the file had since gained; each file's own header was already correct. Nothing gates this (check_line_citations.py only sees line refs). So when moving an op between ops/*.rs submodules, grep the parent mod.rs for the 'mod <target>;' decl and fix that comment in the SAME commit; prefer keeping the decl comment about placement/visibility rationale and letting the file's //! header carry the op inventory, so there is only one copy to rot.
invariant-move-on-symbol-epsilon-result: automaton epsilon-marker contract (angr-9ke6b.191, 2026-08-03): EpsilonNFA::move_on_symbol (native/angr/src/automaton/epsilon_nfa.rs) returns Result<StateSet, EpsilonSymbolError> — it used to assert!(!is_epsilon(symbol)). Reason the Result branch was chosen over the debug_assert! branch the bead also allowed: the ONLY caller chain is PyEpsilonNFA::minimize -> subset_construction -> move_on_symbol, i.e. it is entirely reachable from PyO3, where a Rust panic becomes an opaque PanicException in Python instead of a ValueError. Ripple was cheap (one non-test caller), so subset_construction now returns Result<DFA, EpsilonSymbolError> and PyEpsilonNFA::minimize maps it with PyValueError::new_err(err.to_string()). The invariant itself still holds by construction: EpsilonNFA::add_transition keeps EPSILON out of self.alphabet, and subset_construction only iterates nfa.alphabet(). Rule of thumb this establishes for the .9ke6b assert!-hardening band: pick Result over debug_assert! when the function is PyO3-reachable AND the caller count is small; pick debug_assert! (see angr-9ke6b.182 in dfa.rs) when it is a pure-internal worklist invariant.
invariant-multi-symbolic-bitmap-dispatch: invariant: in native/angr/src/memory/, the page symbolic_bitmap and multi_bitmap are NOT mutually exclusive, and no code may assume they are. A byte promoted Symbolic->Multi keeps BOTH bits set: SymbolicMemory::set_multi_alternatives retires the symbolic_objects entry via retire_symbolic_object_at but never calls MemoryPage::clear_symbolic. Multi wins by DISPATCH ORDER instead -- every reader must probe Multi before Symbolic. Current readers that do: load_concrete_common's range_has_multi gate, assemble_load_with_multi, compute_wider_load_fingerprint, merge::merge_byte_value's is_multi arm. A new reader that checks is_symbolic first will silently resolve a Multi byte to a retired/absent symbolic object. Corollary for readers that only want CONCRETE bytes: is_symbolic alone is not enough, because a cell installed on a never-symbolic byte (install_multi_for_candidates) sets only the multi bit -- SymbolicMemory::read_concrete_bytes_for_lift has to check both, else the lifter decodes MultiPayload::collapse's don't-care concrete_byte default as an instruction byte (angr-4r8mh, fixed). The reverse transition IS asymmetric and must stay so: a symbolic store over a Multi cell DOES clear the multi bit (store_concrete -> clear_multi_at), because there the stale bit would win the dispatch order and shadow the fresh value (angr-0jh0j.31). Pinned by memory::tests::multi::payload::test_multi_supersedes_existing_symbolic, collapse.rs::test_symbolic_overwrite_clears_multi_cell and collapse.rs::test_lift_read_stops_at_multi_byte.
invariant-multi-vs-symbolic-cell-states: After Phase 1.1, an address byte in Rust SymbolicMemory can be in one of four states: (1) pure Concrete (no bitmap bits, no sidecar entries); (2) plain Symbolic (page.is_symbolic bit set, entry in symbolic_objects and/or symbolic_spans, NOT in multi_objects); (3) Multi (page.is_multi bit set, entry in multi_objects, NOT in symbolic_objects — set_multi_alternatives clears the symbolic entries); (4) inconsistent/transitional (any other combination, treated as a bug). The 'Multi supersedes Symbolic' rule is enforced by the set_multi_alternatives setter — see test_multi_supersedes_existing_symbolic in native/angr/src/memory/tests/multi/payload.rs. When transitioning a byte's state, clear the old sidecar entries before installing the new one. BOTH directions have a setter that does this and both MUST be used: Symbolic->Multi is `set_multi_alternatives`, Multi->Symbolic is `clear_multi_at` (drops the multi_objects payload AND the page multi_bitmap bit; safe no-op on a non-Multi byte). Note `MemoryPage::mark_symbolic` alone is NOT enough — it only touches symbolic_bitmap, so a path that marks a byte symbolic without `clear_multi_at` leaves state (4). This exact omission has now been found and fixed at every known Multi->Symbolic transition site, so treat any NEW one as guilty until it calls clear_multi_at: `SymbolicMemory::merge`'s collapse-a-Multi-side-into-an-ITE path (angr-0jh0j.31), `store_concrete`'s symbolic branch (angr-9ke6b.95), and `import_symbolic_value` (angr-6cp06.62 — the live flush_stores / flush_stores_to_rust_memory path, so it silently dropped ordinary symbolic stores at concretized addresses). The failure mode is identical in all three: load_concrete_common's range_has_multi check dispatches Multi-marked bytes to the Multi path BEFORE consulting symbolic_objects, and flush_multi_cells then writes the stale payload back over the new value on export. See also [[invariant-symbolic-byte-lane-lookup]] and [[invariant-every-load-path-gates-multi]].
invariant-native-handler-err-no-rollback: INVARIANT for native procedures/syscalls (native/angr/src/procedures/, syscalls/): returning Err(ProcedureError|SyscallError) does NOT roll back state. Per procedures/mod.rs's dispatch doc (rule 5), Python takes over on the SAME mutated RustSimState, so every mutation the handler already applied is visible to — and re-applied on top of — the Python implementation. Consequence: order a handler so irreversible bookkeeping (heap_free/heap_alloc, fd-table updates, position advances) happens AFTER the fallible work, not before. NativeRealloc (procedures/malloc.rs) hit this in angr-sqfj8.82: it freed the old ptr, then copied; a copy failure would have handed Python a state where ptr was already marked freed. Fixed by moving heap_free below the copy_forward call. What cannot be avoided (the bump-heap allocation made to get a destination address) is leaked and documented in place. Sibling rule to invariant-syscall-fd-check-before-count: both are about statement ORDER inside a handler, and both need a test that drives the failure path and asserts the pre-failure state is still intact.
invariant-native-proc-return-width-exten: A native SimProcedure's return value must be stored via exploration::helpers::write_proc_return_with_abi (or its two thin adapters, CcSnapshot::write_proc_return for the parallel post-step path and RustExplorationManager::write_proc_return for the single-threaded one) -- never via a raw state.set_register_by_offset(return_register, rv). RegisterFile::put writes exactly rv.width()/8 bytes at the offset and leaves the rest of the slot untouched, so a 32-bit int-return BV (printf/puts/open/strcmp/getopt/posix_memalign/fgetc) leaves the caller's stale RAX[63:32] / X0[63:32] alive -- which no real machine does (angr-fs8kb.40). The widening is an ABI fact, CallingConvention::return_extension() -> ReturnExtension::{Zero,Sign}: Zero (hardware sub-register-write semantics) for amd64/AArch64 and inert on the 32-bit ABIs whose return register is already int-wide; Sign for MipsN64, whose ABI requires a 32-bit value in a 64-bit register to be held sign-extended. Two corollaries: (1) adding a new CallingConvention impl means deciding return_extension, not inheriting the default by accident; (2) do NOT 'fix' an int-returning proc by switching it to arch_word() -- that sign-extends everywhere, and an amd64 int return of -1 is 0x00000000FFFFFFFF in RAX, not all-ones. A value already at or above the register width passes through verbatim, so pointer-returning procs and the invariant-wide-return-needs-python-fallback case are unaffected.
invariant-native-stdin-readers-use-mint-: Harness-seeded stdin (posix.stdin.content -> fd 0 content_sym, angr-mb09c) is consumed by exactly ONE helper: procedures/stdin_common.rs::mint_stdin_bytes. It mints the plain 8-bit leaf symbols, eq-binds the seeded prefix by constraint (never stores the seed AST into the guest buffer -- see avoid-storing-extract-asts-in-guest-buffers), and record_stdin_symbol's ONLY the bytes past the seed (recording seeded ones makes _inject_rust_stdin append a duplicate copy of the harness's chunk). Callers: read.rs::read_stdin_symbolic, fgets.rs (fgets/gets/fgetc/getchar), scanf.rs::do_scanf %s path when record_stdin, syscalls/cgc.rs::NativeReceiveSyscall. INVARIANT: any NEW native reader of fd 0 must call mint_stdin_bytes rather than RustBV::symbolic + record_stdin_symbol, or harness-seeded stdin silently regresses to zeros + a zero prefix in posix.dumps(0). Known gap (angr-ptf54): scanf numeric conversions (%d et al.) do NOT consume the seed -- no byte-for-byte mapping exists through a decimal parse, so a seeded harness whose target scanfs %d still gets a fresh symbol and leaves the seed unconsumed. COMPANION (angr-9ke6b.158, commit 24a118286): the NON-stdin side of the same shape lives in syscalls/support.rs -- syscalls::mint_symbolic_bytes (mint N fresh bytes + store into a buffer; used by read_symbolic, scatter_symbolic, cgc random, NativeGetrandomSyscall) and syscalls::fresh_byte_names (the '<prefix>_<id>_<i>' naming half, one counter bump per batch). CGC receive uses fresh_byte_names + mint_stdin_bytes: it needs the names BEFORE the bytes exist, which is exactly why naming is split out of mint_symbolic_bytes. A new fd-0 reader therefore combines both helpers; a new non-fd-0 buffer-filler uses mint_symbolic_bytes alone and must NOT hand-roll the counter/format!/store loop. DISCARD RULE (angr-sqfj8.84): the consume half must run even when the value is thrown away -- scanf's suppressed conversions ('%*s'/'%*c') assign nothing but the real scanf(3) still reads those bytes off the stream, so do_scanf calls mint_stdin_bytes for them too and skips only the memory_store and the conversion-count increment. Any native reader with a 'skip/discard this field' path must consume rather than 'continue', or the fd-0 cursor desyncs and the NEXT conversion re-reads the seed from the wrong offset.
invariant-native-string-scan-python-boun:
Native string procs (strlen.rs, strcmp.rs, strchr.rs and the memchr/memcmp variants) enforce Python's symbolic-scan budget, not just its pruning constraint. Two SEPARATE Python-parity mechanisms, both now present, do not confuse them:
(1) PRUNING — strings::null_exists_constraint asserts 'a null exists in the scanned window', the constraint Python gets free from memory.find (smart_find_mixin._find_process_cases adds Or(*cases)). Landed under angr-sgcye. Called by strlen.rs::scan_for_null (require_null) and strcmp.rs::compare_bytes (only when stop_at_null && its explicit `unbounded` parameter — a caller-bounded strncmp/strncasecmp may legitimately compare n non-null bytes at ANY n, so it must NOT assert this). Deriving `unbounded` from the window length instead was angr-fs8kb.36: `max_len >= MAX_STRCMP_LEN` is also true for strncmp(a,b,4096), which pruned valid unterminated-but-equal buffers. Both flags are now explicit parameters; never re-derive one from max_len.
(2) WINDOW — strings::MAX_SYMBOLIC_SCAN_BYTES = 60, mirroring state.libc.buf_symbolic_bytes (angr/state_plugins/libc.py), which Python passes to memory.find as max_symbolic_bytes; smart_find_mixin._find_iter_items simply RETURNS once that many symbolic chars have been yielded. Enforced inside strings::scan_concrete_then_collect (angr-gorvf.5, commit c94941fff) so every scanner that shares the skeleton inherits it. ONLY symbolic positions draw down the budget — concrete filler is free, exactly as in Python.
WHY THE WINDOW MATTERS: without it a fully-symbolic buffer collected up to MAX=4096 positions, so the ITE chain AND the null_exists_constraint disjunction ran thousands of terms wide, and each term kept a downstream branch feasible -> fork-storm where Python deadends. Pruning alone does NOT fix this; a 4096-wide Or is barely a constraint.
IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: the budget needed no signature change to scan_concrete_then_collect's 6 call sites — the existing `concrete` closure already answers ConcreteStep::BeginCollect exactly for the loads a given scan treats as symbolic, so it doubles as the symbolic predicate during the collect phase.
KNOWN REMAINING DIVERGENCES (both benign, neither a fork-storm driver): Python strlen.py swaps a depth>3 result for a fresh BVS + equality constraint (native returns the raw ITE chain — AST-size cost only); and Python's total search window is max_str_len=128 with doubling, while native still scans concretely to 4096 (strictly more permissive, so it cannot wrongly kill a state).
NULL_EXISTS_CONSTRAINT DETAILS (absorbed in the R4 merge): the helper (procedures/strings.rs::null_exists_constraint, an Or over the symbolic bytes collected by scan_for_null_symbolic / the s1 side of compare_bytes) declines when the window holds a concrete null (trivially true) or holds NO symbolic byte (trivially false - would wrongly kill the state). ONLY sound for the procedure's own MAX window: strnlen legitimately saturates at maxlen and strncmp(a,b,n) may compare n non-null bytes at any n, so the caller-bounded variants pass require_null=false / unbounded=false. Relatedly (angr-fs8kb.36), strncmp/strncasecmp no longer clamp n to MAX_STRCMP_LEN — a clamped window answers for 4096 bytes while claiming to answer for n — so n > MAX defers to Python via check_max, the same shape strnlen already used. Landed commit e370c8331 (angr-sgcye); Python-parity source is procedures/libc/strlen.py's state.memory.find assertion.
